problem:
Which of the following geometric series converge?

- $1+5+25+125+⋯$
- $\frac{2}{7}+\frac{4}{3}+\frac{56}{9}+\frac{784}{27}+⋯$
- $0.1+0.01+0.001+0.000\,1+⋯$

examples.problem:
Which of the following geometric series converge?

- $\displaystyle{\sum_{n = 1}^ \infty} 4 (-3)^{n}$

- $\displaystyle{\sum_{n = 6}^\infty} 32 \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{4n}$

- $\displaystyle{\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}} \dfrac{4^n}{2^{n+3}}$
examples.worked_solution:
Let's look at each series in turn.

- The series $\displaystyle{\sum_{n = 1}^ \infty} 4 (-3)^{n}$ starts with $n=1.$ So the common ratio is

$$
\begin{aligned}r=\frac{{a}_{2}}{{a}_{1}} & =\frac{4(-3)^{2}}{4(-3)^{1}} \\  & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the series is divergent because $|r| \geq 1.$

- The series $\displaystyle{\sum_{n = 6}^\infty} 32 \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{4n}$ starts with $n=6.$ So the common ratio is

$$
\begin{aligned}r=\frac{{a}_{7}}{{a}_{6}} & =\frac{32{(\frac{1}{2})}^{4(7)}}{32{(\frac{1}{2})}^{4(6)}} \\  & =\frac{32{(\frac{1}{2})}^{28}}{32{(\frac{1}{2})}^{24}} \\  & ={(\frac{1}{2})}^{4} \\  & =\frac{1}{16}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the series is convergent because $|r| < 1.$

- The series $\displaystyle{\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}} \dfrac{4^n}{2^{n+3}}$ starts with $n=0.$ So the common ratio is

$$
\begin{aligned}r=\frac{{a}_{1}}{{a}_{0}} & =\frac{(\frac{{4}^{1}}{{2}^{1+3}})}{(\frac{{4}^{0}}{{2}^{0+3}})} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{{4}^{1}}{{2}^{4}})}{(\frac{{4}^{0}}{{2}^{3}})} \\  & =(\frac{{4}^{1}}{{2}^{4}})(\frac{{2}^{3}}{{4}^{0}}) \\  & =\frac{4}{2} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the series is divergent because $|r| \geq 1.$

In conclusion, only series II converges.

feedback.problem:
Which of the following statements is true regarding the series 
 ${\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }(-4){(\frac{3}{4})}^{2n}$ ?
feedback.worked_solution:
The series starts with $n=0.$ So the common ratio is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =\frac{{a}_{1}}{{a}_{0}} \\  & =\frac{(-4){(\frac{3}{4})}^{2(1)}}{(-4){(\frac{3}{4})}^{2(0)}} \\  & =\frac{{(\frac{3}{4})}^{2}}{1} \\  & =\frac{9}{16}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the series is convergent because $|r|<1.$
